summary.short: Mexican electricity regulator's rules on self-consumption (Autoconsumo) of electricity: generation permits, isolated and interconnected schemes, surplus-sale terms, market operation and a self-consumption registry. Binding on permit holders, users, grid operators and market participants from the business day after DOF publication.
summary.long: Administrative rules issued by Mexico's Comisión Nacional de Energía, signed 28 November 2025, implementing the self-consumption (Autoconsumo) figure of the Electricity Sector Law and its regulation. They apply nationwide to permit holders, self-consumption users, grid operators, CENACE, the state supply company and market participants. Chapters II to IV set rules for isolated and interconnected self-consumption, with or without surplus sales, including grid studies, connection contracts, reverse-power protection and storage backup for intermittent generation. Community micro-grids of 0.7 to 5 MW are covered. Chapter V sets minimum contract contents between permit holders and users. Chapter VI governs wholesale market representation and surplus-sale payments, calculated from the levelised cost of the last long-term auction and the local marginal price. Chapter VII requires a Self-Consumption Registry, updated within 15 business days of changes or by 31 March each year. Permits end if users' maximum demand stays below 50% (conventional) or 30% (renewable) of installed capacity for twelve months. Transitional provisions cover existing isolated permits and interim market representation; annexes contain a model surplus-sale contract and the registry form. Infringements are sanctioned under the Electricity Sector Law.
